content: Happiness is the absence of the striving for happiness.
author: Zhuangzi
story:
Refusing lucrative ministerial appointments to remain an impoverished lacquer-garden clerk in Meng, Zhuangzi employed sparkling parables, dreaming butterflies, and irreverent humor to puncture human arrogance. He showed that true freedom lies in wandering at ease with the Tao, transcending rigid social categories of usefulness and uselessness.

In formulating this reflection, Zhuangzi stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of happiness. For Zhuangzi, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
